task_instance: Generate a small AWS Terraform configuration (VPC with private subnets and an S3 bucket with versioning/encryption/public-access-block) laid out and formatted according to the HashiCorp Terraform style guide (terraform.tf, providers.tf, variables.tf, locals.tf, main.tf, outputs.tf; two-space indentation, aligned '=' signs, for_each over count, descriptive singular resource names, every variable/output with type/description, pinned version constraints).
blocker_detail: Secondary check only: full `terraform validate` needs to download the hashicorp/aws provider from registry.terraform.io, which the sandbox's network proxy blocks (host not in the egress allowlist, 403/Forbidden). This does not affect the core deliverable, which was generated and verified by other means.
evidence: Created tf-sample/{terraform.tf,providers.tf,variables.tf,locals.tf,main.tf,outputs.tf} in the work directory following the skill's file-organization table and code style rules (2-space indent, aligned '=', meta-arguments first, for_each for the subnet resources, singular descriptive resource names like aws_vpc.main/aws_s3_bucket.app_data, every variable and output carries description+type, version constraints pinned with '~>'/'>='). Verified formatting compliance with `terraform fmt -recursive -diff` (no changes produced) and `terraform fmt -recursive -check` (exit code 0), confirming the generated HCL already matches canonical Terraform formatting. Attempted `terraform init`/`terraform validate` for full semantic validation; this failed only because registry.terraform.io is not in the sandbox's network allowlist ('Host not in allowlist: registry.terraform.io'), a network restriction unrelated to the code-generation deliverable itself. Manually cross-checked the generated files against the skill's Code Review Checklist (file organization, naming, variables/outputs documented, for_each usage, version pinning, tagging via locals) and all items are satisfied.
